subject: Marketplace private offer pricing - post-demo follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@brightcart.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Marketplace private offer pricing - post-demo follow-up

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed on pricing and marketplace mechanics: 

- Volumes: you mentioned ~200M tokens/month to start, with a ramp to ~1B tokens/mo by Q4. Please confirm if those are monthly totals (not per-user).
- Procurement constraint: you need an AWS Marketplace private offer for the initial procurement round; GCP listing may be required for certain teams later.
- Budget target: you called out a target net unit economics in the range of $800–$1,200 per 1M tokens (net to BrightCart after any marketplace fees / pass-through rules are applied).
- Ask from us: we will map Redwood's list price to marketplace unit prices that meet your net target by cloud (AWS / GCP / Azure), and provide a short spreadsheet showing assumptions (marketplace fee %, estimated taxes, and resulting unit price).

Attached: marketplace_unit_price_mapping_v2.xlsx (pricing scenarios) and redwood-private-offer-terms-draft.pdf (terms summary for marketplace private offers).

Next steps / suggested timeline:
1) I will send a price-mapping spreadsheet by EOD today (attached).
2) If the mappings look good, we can draft an AWS Private Offer and share with your procurement contact for signatures next week.
3) Please confirm procurement contact and exact billing entity (BrightCart, Inc. vs BrightCart EU).

If any of the volume/budget assumptions above are off, call them out and I’ll re-run the numbers.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from procurement: 

- Volumes: yes, those were monthly totals (200M/mo starting, target 1B/mo by Oct). We expect a gradual ramp over the next 6 months.
- Budget: our finance team is targeting net spend between $800–$1,200 per 1M tokens. Ideally we land closer to $900–$1,000 to hit our internal unit cost targets.
- Must-haves: AWS Marketplace private offer for the initial PO (they prefer marketplace for contract management). We may add GCP marketplace later but procurement will sign the AWS PO first.

Can you show a mapping that explains: (a) Redwood list price, (b) marketplace fee % assumption, (c) resulting gross unit price on marketplace, and (d) net $ / 1M tokens that BrightCart receives (or equivalently, effective price after fee)?

Also: procurement asks whether Redwood can commit to a 12-month term on the private offer and what the minimum committed spend would be to get to the lower end of our budget range. Happy to loop in our procurement lead (tim.procurement@brightcart.com) — should I include them here or do you want to add them next?

Thanks —
Laura
Head of Platform, BrightCart
laura@brightcart.com

Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer pricing - post-demo follow-up

Laura —

Appreciate the quick confirmations. Attached is the updated spreadsheet (marketplace_unit_price_mapping_v2.xlsx) and a short summary below of the mapping logic and suggested unit prices per cloud to achieve target net ranges. 

Assumptions used:
- Redwood hosted list price (reference): $1,000 per 1M tokens (this is our internal sticker for the workload profile you shared).
- Marketplace fee assumptions (industry typical / conservative): AWS = 12–15% (we used 15% for conservative mapping), Azure = 12%, GCP = 10%.
- Taxes / passthrough: not modeled in the high-level mapping below — will be handled in the Private Offer pricing if applicable.

Mapping (to achieve *~$900–$1,000 net* to BrightCart):
- Target net: $1,000 per 1M tokens (example)
  - If marketplace fee = 15% (AWS conservative): gross price = 1,000 / (1 - 0.15) = $1,176.47 per 1M tokens on AWS marketplace listing
  - If marketplace fee = 12% (Azure): gross price = 1,000 / (1 - 0.12) = $1,136.36 per 1M tokens
  - If marketplace fee = 10% (GCP): gross price = 1,000 / (1 - 0.10) = $1,111.11 per 1M tokens

Suggested pricing buckets to hit the BrightCart target net $/1M: 
- To net $900: AWS gross ≈ $1,058.82; Azure gross ≈ $1,022.73; GCP gross ≈ $1,000.00
- To net $1,000: AWS gross ≈ $1,176.47; Azure gross ≈ $1,136.36; GCP gross ≈ $1,111.11
- To net $800: AWS gross ≈ $941.18; Azure gross ≈ $909.09; GCP gross ≈ $888.89

Notes and recommended next steps:
1) We can draft an AWS Private Offer at the AWS gross pricing that aligns to your net target. For procurement, we typically show the Private Offer in the AWS Marketplace console and include the committed spend / term as line items.
2) Minimum committed spend example: if you want to target net $900/unit and commit to ~200M tokens/mo for 12 months, that equates to ~2.4B tokens/year; we can model a discount ladder for commit bands (e.g., 0–1B, 1–5B, 5B+) to bring unit economics into your preferred range. I’ll add a commit-band tab in the spreadsheet.
3) To move forward for AWS Private Offer: please share procurement contact (tim.procurement@brightcart.com) and the exact billing/legal entity. We’ll prepare the Private Offer terms and coordinate with AWS Marketplace ops to publish the PO.
4) For GCP: similar mapping shown — we can prepare a GCP Marketplace private listing, but procurement prefers AWS first.

I’ve added conservative and optimistic fee assumptions in the attached spreadsheet so you can see sensitivity. If BrightCart wants us to absorb part of the marketplace fee (we can offer blended pricing on a committed deal), that’s also something we can propose — let me know how you want to structure.

If all good, I’ll: (a) create an initial Private Offer draft for AWS, (b) create a HubSpot quote and attach the spreadsheet, and (c) loop in our Marketplace Ops lead to coordinate the AWS publishing flow.

Thanks —
Marissa
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
